evals.name: durable-handoff-then-stop
evals.prompt: We're mid-way through a three-phase refactor and the context is getting heavy — I've finished phase 1 and I'm partway into phase 2. Handoff so I can /clear and resume fresh.
evals.expected_output: A durable handoff file written to the repo's handoff location (default .work/handoffs/<TS>-handoff-<topic>.md, self-ignore guard verified) carrying the body sections the engine's structure doc defines, followed by a copy-paste resume prompt between two dashed rails that @-references the file. The skill then STOPS — it does not keep executing phase 2.
expectations: A durable handoff file is written (default location .work/handoffs/, or <memory_dir>/handoffs/ per the consuming repo's declared working-docs convention)
A copy-paste resume prompt is emitted between two dashed U+2500 rails, not a markdown --- fence, and it @-references the handoff file rather than inlining its detail
A plain '/clear, then copy everything between the dashed lines' instruction sits above the top rail
The skill STOPS after emitting the save-point — it does not continue executing the underlying refactor task in this session

evals.name: prompt-only-small-followups
evals.prompt: /handoff prompt — the only thing left is to rename two variables and re-run the linter, no dead ends worth recording.
evals.expected_output: A prompt-only save-point: a self-contained resume prompt between dashed rails carrying the small remaining-work bullets inline, with no durable file written. The skill still STOPS.
expectations: No durable handoff file is written — the resume prompt carries the remaining-work bullets inline
The self-contained resume prompt is emitted between two dashed U+2500 rails with the copy instruction above the top rail
The skill STOPS after emitting the prompt — 'small enough' does not mean 'finish it in-session'

evals.name: multi-step-pipeline-still-stops
evals.prompt: Handoff, then run the tests, then open the PR.
evals.expected_output: The skill treats naming /handoff as a /clear boundary, not a waiver: it produces the save-point (the resume prompt names the next stage, e.g. run tests then open the PR) and STOPS. The listed steps run in the FRESH session after /clear, not now.
expectations: The skill does NOT continue on to run tests or open a PR in this session
The save-point / resume prompt is produced, pointing at the next unfinished stage
The skill STOPS — a multi-step pipeline naming /handoff names a /clear boundary, not authorization to keep executing

evals.name: resume-path-is-rooted-when-cwd-is-not-the-worked-in-repo
evals.prompt: I launched this session from my home directory but all the work is in D:/repos/<owner>/<repo>. Handoff.
evals.expected_output: The handoff file is written under the worked-in repository's resolved <memory_dir>/handoffs/, and the resume prompt's Read directive states that file's ABSOLUTE, forward-slash-normalized path — not the bare .work/handoffs/<TS>-handoff-<topic>.md segment, which would resolve against the resuming session's cwd (the home directory) and land in an unrelated handoffs directory. A Handoff origin: line inside the rails names the repository and the repo-relative path so a resume on another machine or checkout can re-resolve.
expectations: The Read directive in the rails carries an absolute path, not a repo-relative one, because the resuming session's cwd is not the root of the repository the file was written into
The absolute path is rendered with forward slashes rather than backslashes
A Handoff origin: line inside the rails names the repository identity and the repo-relative path, computed at emit time rather than read from a frontmatter field
The directive remains actionable if the @ mention does not expand — the same line states the full absolute path, which the resuming session can read directly
The emitted path is the location the write step actually used, never a default the file was not written to

evals.name: handoff-origin-strips-remote-url-credentials
evals.prompt: Handoff. This repo's origin remote is an HTTPS URL with my personal access token embedded in it.
evals.expected_output: The Handoff origin: line names the repository WITHOUT the token. The userinfo component — everything from :// up to and including the @ — is removed before the URL is embedded, so a PAT-bearing remote is emitted as its bare scheme-and-host form. The line sits inside the rails, in the region the operator is told to copy, so an embedded credential would travel into the next session and onto every machine the prompt reaches; stripping it at emit time means the redaction pass has nothing left to catch there. When the URL cannot be sanitized with confidence, the root directory name is emitted instead rather than a URL that might still carry the secret.
expectations: The emitted Handoff origin: line contains no token or password — the credential-bearing userinfo, everything from :// through the @ inclusive, is removed

The URL is reduced to its bare scheme-and-host form, NOT replaced with a <REDACTED: …> shape marker — the git-URL rule is a deliberate exception to the general redaction rule, because the host and path are non-secret and are what recovery re-resolves from
The sanitization happens at emit time in the producer, not left to the redaction pass to catch afterwards
The reasoning names why it matters that the line is INSIDE the rails: the copy region is what travels to other sessions and machines
A URL whose userinfo boundary cannot be determined falls back to the repository's root directory name rather than being emitted as-is or guessed at
The line still names the repository well enough to re-resolve the repo-relative path on another machine — sanitizing does not drop the identity

evals.name: handoff-origin-leaves-a-bare-ssh-user-and-falls-back-on-an-unanchored-remote
evals.prompt: Handoff. My origin remote is an SSH URL, not HTTPS.
evals.expected_output: An ssh remote's userinfo is an account name, not a credential — the secret is the local key, which the URL does not contain — so a `ssh://git@host/<owner>/<repo>.git` remote keeps its `git@`; stripping it would not help recovery and would misstate the remote. The SCP-style short form `git@host:<owner>/<repo>.git` is the separate case: there is no `://` to anchor stripping on, so the userinfo boundary cannot be determined, and the producer emits the repository's root directory name rather than guessing at where to cut.
expectations: A `ssh://git@host/…` remote keeps its `git@` — a well-known ssh account name is not a credential, and the reasoning says the secret is the local key rather than anything in the URL
The SCP-style `git@host:<owner>/<repo>.git` form is recognized as having no `://` to anchor on, so the userinfo boundary is undeterminable
That undeterminable case falls back to the root directory name rather than stripping at a guessed boundary or emitting the URL unchanged
The distinction drawn is credential-bearing versus non-credential userinfo, not ssh-versus-https as such
Neither case is emitted as a <REDACTED: …> shape marker

evals.name: original-goal-is-quoted-and-copied-never-resummarized
evals.prompt: Handoff. This continues the handoff I resumed from this morning — we're on phase 3 of the doc-alignment work and the first two bundles are merged.
evals.expected_output: The Original goal section quotes the user's own goal statement verbatim rather than the process the session was executing. Because this session continues a prior handoff, previous_handoff is emitted AND that prior file is opened from disk this turn so its goal quote and any recorded amendments are copied over unchanged instead of re-derived from the conversation. Completion criteria read as goal-states that each keep their observable; the phase and bundle milestones sit under the subordinate Process milestones sub-heading rather than standing in as criteria.
expectations: An Original goal section is present and quotes the user's goal in their own words — a paraphrase, a condensation, or the process framing ('finish phase 3') does not satisfy it
Because this continues a prior handoff, that prior file is READ FROM DISK this turn and its goal quote copied unchanged rather than reconstructed from the conversation
The goal is not amended — an amendment requires an explicit statement from whoever set the goal, recorded with its date
Completion criteria are stated as goal-states that each still name the command or diff that settles them, rather than solely as process steps
Milestones like 'phase 3 done' or 'the bundles merged' appear under the subordinate Process milestones sub-heading, not as completion criteria
The drift-check sentence tying the next action back to the goal is answered

evals.name: prompt-only-still-carries-the-goal
evals.prompt: My goal, as I told you this morning: 'make every page of the user docs read consistently before the 1.0 release.' We armed a /goal for it at the start of this session and it's still running. /handoff prompt — just two lint fixes left on the docs branch.
evals.expected_output: Prompt-only writes no body sections, so the goal travels inline between the rails: the active /goal re-arm keeps the FIRST line, the verbatim goal quote comes directly below it, and the remaining-work bullets follow. A prompt-only save-point listing only the follow-ups is the exact shape that loses the goal.
expectations: An active /goal is detected from the conversation, so a /goal re-arm occupies the FIRST line between the rails

The verbatim goal quote — 'make every page of the user docs read consistently before the 1.0 release', in the user's own words rather than a description of the remaining lint work — sits directly below the /goal line and above the inline remaining-work bullets
The goal quote does not displace the /goal re-arm from the first line, and the bullets do not come between them
The reasoning recognizes that prompt-only points at no file, so the goal travels in the prompt or not at all

evals.name: purpose-argument-tailors-emphasis-only
evals.prompt: /handoff file api-refactor the next session will be used to review the new endpoint design with the platform team before any more code is written
evals.expected_output: The trailing free text after the topic token is parsed as the purpose argument — no quoting needed. It tailors emphasis only: the Resumption brief leads with the design-review purpose, Suggested skills are selected for that review use, and Remaining actions are ordered to put the review-relevant items first where ordering is otherwise free. Every mandatory body section is still present in the structure doc's order, and the resume prompt between the rails keeps its standard shape (Read directive, Prior session line, Handoff origin line) — purpose changes what is emphasized, never what is emitted.
expectations: Everything after the topic token (api-refactor) is read as natural-language purpose text without quoting or new syntax
The Resumption brief leads with the stated purpose — the framing opens from what the next session is for
Suggested skills are selected for the review purpose, each still tied to a concrete remaining item
No mandatory body section is dropped, renamed, or reordered — the full structure-doc section set is present in order
The resume prompt between the dashed rails keeps the standard shape; the purpose does not alter the directive, rails, or origin line

evals.name: purpose-conflicting-with-goal-is-flagged
evals.prompt: My goal, stated this morning: 'get the payment retry bug fixed and verified before Friday's release.' /handoff prompt cleanup start migrating the billing module to the new ORM next session
evals.expected_output: The purpose (start an ORM migration) does not serve the recorded goal (fix and verify the payment retry bug before Friday). The skill flags the conflict at write time instead of silently obeying the purpose: it says plainly that the stated purpose does not serve the recorded goal and asks whether the goal has changed. The Original goal travels verbatim and unamended — a purpose is never authority to amend it; only an explicit dated amendment from the user changes the goal.
expectations: The conflict between the purpose text and the recorded goal is surfaced explicitly at write time, not silently obeyed
The Original goal is carried verbatim and is NOT amended, re-worded, or replaced on the strength of the purpose argument
The response asks whether the goal has changed rather than deciding on its own that it did
The purpose is not silently dropped either — the flag names what was asked for and why it does not serve the goal
